_comment: Copy to config.json (gitignored) for machine-local global settings. Non-secret defaults live in config.defaults.json (committed); config.json overrides them (shallow top-level merge). notificationChannel is where heartbeat notifications go: slack (slackWebhookUrl, a Slack incoming webhook) or ntfy (ntfyTopic on ntfyServerUrl - blank means https://ntfy.sh - with an optional ntfyToken for a protected topic). notificationEvents is which notifications actually go out - keys from the checkbox list in Settings > Notifications, empty means none. All of it is re-read at send time, so a change applies without restarting the heartbeat. heartbeatMaxAttempts blocks a ticket after that many no-progress heartbeat resumes; heartbeatWorkerTimeoutMinutes kills a worker that has run that long; heartbeatWorkerStallMinutes kills one whose agent has said nothing for that long, which usually means one tool call never returned (0 = off); heartbeatProjects (empty = all) limits which projects the heartbeat works, and heartbeatPriorities (empty = all) limits which priority bands it claims from - TicketPriority names, e.g. ['Critical','High']. Tickets outside either set are passed over, not blocked. baseBranch is the branch new feature branches fork from; branchPrefix prefixes auto-created branch names (e.g. 'jb/').
_comment_heartbeatWorkers: How many agents the one orchestrator runs at once, 1 to 3. It fills slots only when there is work for them, so this is a ceiling and not a target - set it to 1 to go back to the single-agent pipeline without changing anything else. Three is the hard maximum (HeartbeatManager.MaxWorkers); every agent is a full Claude session drawing on the same rate-limit window and the same machine.
_comment_resourceCapacity: How many workers may hold a shared resource at once (see phaseResources in each project.defaults.json). Anything not listed allows exactly one, which is the point of a lease. This is also where a fleet-wide worker cap goes once more than one runs at a time: name a resource 'claude:slot', give it the capacity you want, and require it from every phase - N leases IS an N-worker limit, with no code change.
_comment_worktreeRetentionDays: How long a ticket's worktree is kept after the ticket reaches Done. Past that it is removed on the next start of the app, or the next daily pass - the directory only: the branch stays, and a worktree with uncommitted or untracked files is never removed. 0 keeps every worktree until someone removes it by hand.
_comment_agentProvider: Which agent CLI the heartbeat drives: 'claude' (Claude Code), 'codex' (OpenAI Codex) or 'gemini' (Google Gemini CLI). The CLI has to be installed and signed in - `claude`, `codex login`, or `gemini` once interactively (or a GEMINI_API_KEY in the environment). Anything unrecognised falls back to claude. Switching provider also switches which model names are valid: a workerModel that unmistakably belongs to a different provider is replaced with the new provider's default rather than passed through, so you cannot strand the fleet on a model its CLI will reject. NOTE: the gemini provider was written from Google's documentation and has never been run - expect to fix something the first time you select it.
_comment_phaseModels: Per-phase overrides of workerModel, keyed by skill name: speculate, implement, qa-test, refine. A phase left out (or set to "") runs workerModel, so this only ever changes the phases you name. Use it to spend a more capable model where the leverage is - speculation writes the plan every later phase implements, and is a small fraction of a ticket's runs - without moving the phases that are working. Same model names as workerModel; one belonging to the other provider is dropped, exactly as workerModel's is.
_comment_workerReasoningEffort: How hard EVERY agent run is asked to think - each phase, reflection, the Classroom analysis and walkthrough, and the improvement applier - for providers exposing that as a dial (claude --effort, codex model_reasoning_effort: low|medium|high|xhigh). The Gemini CLI has no such flag and ignores this - Gemini's thinking is a property of the model you pick. Empty means medium, not the CLI's own default: Claude Code's default moves with the model (Opus 5: high, Opus 5.5: medium).
